route: E6 probe: second bridge from zeta23
detail: NOT dischargeable from zeta23 as-is: Zeta23 states only the dyadic clause |N(T,2T) - (T/2pi) l1(T)| <= C log T plus the local count; summing dyadic windows gives an O(log^2 T) remainder, so the O(log T) cumulative statement is not a corollary. An O(log T) cumulative bound IS derivable from its general-window lemmas (folded argument principle at good heights, Gamma-side integral of mu, Backlund at any good height, Stirling for mu) but needs a new general-interval Stirling integral + two local-count corrections (~ hundreds of lines) -- not attempted, not faked. Multiplicity reconciliation (Mathlib divisor = analytic order on the open strip; 7/8 and T >= 2 absorbed into C) is written up in E6_PROBE_2026-09-17.md. Native A4 remains the path; zeta23 lemmas are the starting toolkit.

route: blind read-back (blind-auditor-b7) + integrator errata fixes
detail: AUDIT CLEAN, node promoted draft -> open. TWO ERRATA FIXED: (1) the generated BombieriLagarias registry comment claimed the missing Function.update would zero every eta_j with j >= 1 and break the statement for n >= 2; the auditor proved in Lean that eta_0 vanishes too (deriv returns junk at the pole), so it breaks already at n = 1 — corrected in build_rhdefs.py and regenerated; (2) memo section 5 gave the truncation tail as n/gamma^2 while its own section 2.1 gives n^2/gamma^2 — the n^2 law is correct (measured to four significant figures at n = 1..4) and section 5 is corrected. COMPOSITION SEAM, the finding that matters for consumers: B7-i (RH_bl_finite_multiset, proved) hands back an n that DEPENDS ON THE WINDOW T, and its own nonvacuity record says no bounded universal n exists. So B7-i and this node compose in the EASY direction of Li s criterion only; the hard direction needs a uniform-in-T truncation bound, which the memo queues but does NOT register. B10 cannot close Li s criterion from these two nodes alone. conjecture1_proved = False.
